title: chaotic-warmup-spectroscopy-and-load-harness-journal
content:
Purpose
Quick notes and experiments exploring non-deterministic warmup effects (what I'm calling "spectroscopy") on throughput claims. Trying to capture a small repeatable set of procedures, a config vocabulary, and an observation checklist so later runs are comparable. This is intentionally messy — notes-to-self + experiments + TODOs.

Summary / hypothesis
- Hypothesis: small differences in request timing patterns, RNG seed, and background GPU microstate (thermal/clock governors) create measurable +-10-30% throughput variance for the same nominal concurrency.
- Goal: design a harness that (a) reports a reproducible baseline throughput band, (b) isolates major contributors (ipv, seed, thermal), (c) provides a minimal priming recipe to get into a stable steady-state for claimable numbers.

Key concepts introduced here
- Spectroscopy: sweep of controlled perturbations (arrival jitter, seed entropy, small bursts) to characterize stability 'modes'.
- Occupancy priming: not just filling KV caches but occupying CUDA SM resources and memory pools in a reproducible way.
- Chaotic warmup: intentional, randomized short bursts to speed convergence but measured for variance impact.

Minimum observables to capture per run (must be in every result archive)
- harness config (json blob) including client concurrency, arrival distribution, sequence length dist, rng_seed
- host snapshot: kernel driver version, docker image tag, commit SHAs, model artifact sha
- GPU snapshot timeline: nvidia-smi sampling at 1s, DCGM counters (compute util, sm_efficiency, mem_used, power), GPU clocks, GPU temp, fan, perf metrics if available
- process-level traces: latency histograms (p50/p90/p99), tail traces with trace ids, backlog queue lengths, batch sizes emitted by runtime
- system noise: top -b output, iostat, dmesg excerpt for the run period

Harness config examples (vocab we use)
- arrival_profile: {steady | poisson(lambda=...) | jittered-burst(period=60s, burst_qps=..)| staircase(steps=...)}
- concurrency_mode: closed_loop (maintain p50 < X ms), open_loop (fixed qps), sessioned (affinity clients session tokens)
- seed_mode: fixed-seed=<int> | entropy-per-client | time-seed
- priming_sequence: none | deterministic-prefixes | chaotic-spectroscopy(seed=..., bursts=10, width=2s)

Example run (copyable)
- name: run-2026-03-01-chaos-a
- arrival_profile: jittered-burst(period=30s, burst_qps=1200, base_qps=400, sigma=0.12)
- concurrency_mode: open_loop
- seed_mode: fixed-seed=42
- priming_sequence: chaotic-spectroscopy(seed=99, bursts=8, width=3s)
- client_setup: 8 workers per client, 3 clients, tokenized prompt bank of 5k exemplars

Notes from runs (observations)
- Fixed-seed runs reduce throughput variance in short runs (<5m) but increase systematic bias: some seeds align better with batch coalescing in our runtime.
- Chaotic priming reduces time to reach median throughput by ~40% versus deterministic-prefix priming but increases p99 variability during the first 2 minutes.
- Thermal transitions (GPU clock downscaling) observed around minute ~12 on older A100s when ambient temp > 28C; that corresponded with 10–15% throughput dip. Need ambient and thermal baseline in metadata.

Repro checklist (for anyone running a claimable benchmark)
- [ ] Single-run name includes date, harness-commit, model-sha, seed mode
- [ ] Capture and upload GPU/DCGM timeline + harness config to artifact storage
- [ ] Disable background cron jobs on nodes; set cpuset and docker cpu shares to pinned values
- [ ] Set network link shaping deterministic (tc netem off) or record it precisely
- [ ] Run 3 independent runs with different seeds (if seed_mode != fixed) or same-seed repeated 3x for fixed-seed
- [ ] Compare runs using the provided scripts (diff-metrics.sh) and annotate run notes

Instrumentation tips (practical)
- Always sample nvidia-smi at 1s and DCGM at 250–500ms where possible. Lightweight perf counters are good but measure their overhead.
- Correlate buffer/kv cache hits from runtime logs with early reduced batch sizes — that often explains rising throughput curves.
- Capture client-side inter-arrival times and server side request enqueue timestamps to compute client-induced jitter.

Decisions to make / open questions
- Do we standardize on closed-loop for benchmark claims? Closed-loop is more application-realistic but masks raw throughput ceilings. We may publish both: open_loop ceiling + closed_loop SLOable throughput.
- How to represent quantized models versus fp16 in the same benchmark table? Propose separate rows and an explicit quantization_flag in harness metadata.
- Should we include a small synthetic prefix corpus for priming that approximates typical token distributions per model family? Pro: more realistic priming; Con: reduces repeatability if corpus changes. Solution: shard the corpus and check-in the corpus shard used.

Mini runbook (step-by-step)
1) Provision target nodes and pin their kernel/drivers (document exact versions).
2) Push harness binary and harness-commit tag to nodes.
3) Prepare client bank (tokenizer version pinned, prompt shard selected).
4) Pre-warm step (optional): deterministic-prefixes for 90s to fill KV caches.
5) Spectroscopy step: run chaotic-spectroscopy for N bursts (default 8). Observe metrics and annotate.
6) Main run(s): collect full timeline + logs + traces.
7) Post-check: run analysis scripts, produce bandwidth / throughput / p99 plots and an occupancy heatmap per GPU.

Analysis artifacts we want to produce per experiment
- Throughput band (median +- std) over stable window (configurable)
- Spectral plot: throughput vs time with overlaid bursts and thermal/clock events
- Occupancy heatmap: client concurrency x time -> GPU SM occupancy bucketed
- Seed-sensitivity matrix: seed vs median throughput (heatmap)
- Report JSON: keys for claim, artifacts location, commit SHAs, contact owner

TODOs
- Add small harness extension to snapshot OS governor states and write a short string into run metadata.
- Automate thermal baseline capture before a benchmark (idle for 5m).
- Decide canonical stable-window duration (default 5m after priming) and add to harness default config.

Links / references
- Benchmark harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness/pull/412
- Related experiment folder: confluence:serving-runtime/bench-warmup-guides
- Jira for publishing rules: JIRA-ENG-1287

Notes to self: keep these runs cheap but defensible. We need ergonomics for SREs to reproduce a claim in <90m. If thermal noise is frequent, add a standard warm room protocol (or transfer to cooler racks).

-- Aisha
